Try the Galloway method: jog for 1 minute, walk for 2 minutes, and repeat for 20–25 minutes total. Do this 3 times per week. By week 6, you will likely find yourself able to run for 10–15 minutes straight. Key rules: run slow enough to hold a conversation, invest in proper running shoes (not walking shoes), and never increase total weekly running time by more than 10%. Step 2: Categorize each into Keep, Pause, or Cut. Any service you have not actively used in the last 30 days goes to Cut immediately. For the Pause pile, set a calendar reminder for 30 days out; if you have not used it by then, cancel it. Step 3: To prevent future creep, set up a standing rule — no new subscription without cancelling an existing one first (the \"one in, one out\" policy). Practical tips: use a dedicated email alias for sign-ups so they all land in one folder, enable 2FA removal restrictions on your payment methods if your bank offers it, and run this audit on the first of every quarter. Here is your 3-week plan: Week 1 — Skim every chapter looking only at headings, bold terms, summaries, and end-of-chapter questions. Create a one-page \"battle sheet\" per chapter with key concepts only. Week 2 — For each chapter, close the book and write down everything you remember from that battle sheet. Review every wrong answer and understand why it was wrong — those are your highest-yield study moments. During all three weeks, use spaced repetition: review older chapters for 15 minutes at the end of each study session rather than re-reading them.
